findings: [major] vulnerability — A live-looking partner API credential is committed in source. Anyone with repository access can reuse it against the billing API; revoke/rotate it and load the replacement from secret storage. Affected: billing/reconcile.py:1.

[major] data-integrity — The loop starts at index 1, omitting the first ledger row. For the supplied 10/20/30 rows, expected_total=60 incorrectly returns false, while expected_total=50 incorrectly returns true. Affected: billing/reconcile.py:7.

[major] runtime-failure — No definition or import for http_client appears in the reviewed code, so fetch_partner_balance("p-1") raises NameError before making a request. Affected: billing/reconcile.py:14.

[major] missing-validation — partner_id is interpolated directly into a privileged URL path. An input such as ../admin/audit can escape the intended partner-resource path when the client or server normalizes dot segments, sending the bearer credential to another internal endpoint. Validate the identifier and URL-encode it as one path segment. Affected: billing/reconcile.py:15.

[minor] failure-handling — The request has no timeout. If the partner service accepts the connection but never responds, the billing worker can remain blocked indefinitely. Affected: billing/reconcile.py:14.

[minor] failure-handling — HTTP status and response shape are unchecked. A 401/503 error body or a 200 response without a numeric balance produces JSON/KeyError failures or returns invalid data without a controlled partner-service error. Affected: billing/reconcile.py:18.

[major] test-coverage — The new public network function has no test. Locking assertion: with a mocked client, fetch_partner_balance("p-1") must call only /partners/p-1/balance and return a numeric balance on 200, while non-2xx or malformed responses must raise the defined controlled error. Affected: billing/test_reconcile.py:11.
result.summary: Critical (2/10): the diff exposes a credential, introduces incorrect ledger reconciliation, and adds an inadequately protected external-service boundary.
verification: The supplied positive reconciliation test would fail because the implementation sums 20 + 30 rather than 10 + 20 + 30.
Pre-verdict gate: the replay explicitly provides no real repository or PR beyond the frozen diff, so there was no external claim that could be verified without inventing unavailable context.
